sections.h2: Where Mercer County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
The Mercer County Recorder of Deeds is in Suite 109 of the courthouse complex at 125 S. Diamond Street in the borough of Mercer, the county seat. The phone number is 724-662-3800. The counter is open weekdays, 8:30 to 4:30, except holidays.

The same counter takes deeds, mortgages, leases, powers of attorney, easements, subdivision plans and notary bonds. For a house sale the order is simple: the deed is signed at closing, a Uniform Parcel Identifier is certified, and the closing agent files the deed with the transfer tax and the fee. Recordings can be checked online through the Land Records Search on the county website, with the index and images going back to 1972.

Sellers in Sharon, Grove City, Greenville, Hermitage or Farrell all record through this one office. School district names matter on a deed because local transfer tax can be shared with the district. The county is served by Commodore Perry, Farrell Area, Greenville Area, Grove City Area, Hermitage, Jamestown Area, Lakeview, Mercer Area, Reynolds, Sharon City, Sharpsville Area, West Middlesex Area and Wilmington Area, so the property description should place the parcel in the right municipality and district.

Mercer County certifies a Uniform Parcel Identifier for every document that affects title before it can be recorded. The commissioners passed Ordinance No. 2026-001 on November 20, 2025, and it took effect on January 5, 2026.

The UPI is the county tax parcel number already assigned to the property. The Tax Assessment Office certifies it. A document mailed or e-recorded to the Recorder is forwarded there first, so the identifier is settled before the deed reaches the Recorder's desk.

  • The charge is $20.00 for each UPI certification, paid separately to Mercer County Tax Assessment, not to the Recorder.
  • Including the parent parcel number costs nothing extra.
  • When only part of a property is being conveyed, two UPI numbers are needed: one for the new piece and one for the parent parcel.
  • Deeds, quitclaim deeds, mortgages, releases, easements, leases, court decrees and powers of attorney to sell are all covered.
  • Questions and pre-approval requests go to upi@mercercountypa.gov.

To keep your closing on schedule, send the draft deed to the Assessment Office well before the signing date.

A deed costs $71.25 under the fee bill revised June 15, 2026. That base fee includes four pages, four names and one parcel. The county adds $2.00 for each extra page and $0.50 for each extra parcel or name.

Mercer County Recorder of Deeds fee bill, revised June 15, 2026
Document or itemFee
Deed, including corrective deed and decree of distribution$71.25
Mortgage, including amendments and subordinations$71.25
Mortgage assignment, release, satisfaction$59.75
Easement or right of way agreement$71.25
Power of attorney$18.50
Realty transfer tax Statement of Value$2.00 extra
Copies made by staff$0.50 per page
Return of a rejected document$5.00 first time, $10 second, $20 after

The Statement of Value is not part of the four-page base fee. Bring the original plus one copy.

Payment is by cash or check only, and each check needs the account holder's current address and phone number. Enclose a stamped return envelope so the recorded deed goes back to the right buyer.

The baseline is 1 percent to the Commonwealth plus 1 percent local. Five places charge a different local rate, and the recorder collects the whole amount when the deed is filed.

  • Hermitage: 2.5 percent local
  • Sharon: 2.5 percent local
  • Farrell: 2 percent local
  • Greenville: 2 percent local
  • Sheakleyville: 1 percent local, effective May 1, 2019

A deed that covers land in more than one municipality has to state how the transfer tax is divided or what percentage goes to each. The fee bill prints a common level ratio factor of 9.52 for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Under state revenue rules, grantor and grantee both stand behind the tax. Some family transfers, deeds to government bodies and inherited property are exempt from the state tax.

The office rejects paper that does not meet its standards, and a rejected document costs the return fee shown in the table. Check your deed against this list before closing.

  • Original documents only, with an acknowledgment date that does not come before the date of the document.
  • A 2-inch blank margin at the top of every page for the Recorder's stamp.
  • The municipality, county and state of the property written on deeds and mortgages.
  • A signed certificate of residence on deeds, mortgages, articles of agreement and assignments.
  • No highlighting, and text legible enough to index and copy.
  • When several documents belong to one transaction, a note on each showing the order of recording.

The county also requires either the transfer tax or a fully completed Statement of Value on the current Pennsylvania form.

sections.h2: Steps to get a Mercer County deed recorded
sections.html:
In a normal sale the steps run in a fixed order. First the draft deed goes to the Tax Assessment Office so the UPI can be certified and its $20.00 fee paid. Next the deed is signed and acknowledged at closing, and the acknowledgment date must not come before the date of the document. The closing agent then files it at Suite 109 or by e-recording, with the transfer tax and the recording fee, a Statement of Value if one is needed, and a stamped return envelope. Last, the recorded deed is mailed back and the title appears in the online index.

If anything on the document fails the standards above, it comes back with a rejection fee and your closing date can slip, so most agents review it a few days ahead.

sections.h2: How the reassessment affects a sale
sections.html:
The last countywide reassessment finished in 1971. Its replacement was pushed back a year, so new assessed values now take effect for the 2028 tax year instead of 2027. In 2027 each owner will receive a Final Value Mailer showing land, improvements and the total.

A reassessment is designed not to raise total tax revenue. The county, municipalities and school districts are to bill the same total after the change, so millage drops where values rise. As a seller, you can tell a buyer that the value is likely to be reset soon and that the bill may move in either direction.

Once the mailer arrives, you can appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals, and formal appeals must be finished by October 31 of the appeal year. For the current tax picture on a parcel, call the Assessment Office at 724-662-7551 or use the county's GIS parcel viewer, which shows the county, municipal and school bills separately.

Mercer County is in northwest Pennsylvania along the Ohio line, and Hermitage is its largest city. Interstates 79, 80 and 376 and US routes 19 and 62 cross the county. Parcel, school district and municipality decide your transfer tax, so confirm all three before you quote a net figure to a buyer.

faqs.q: How much is the Mercer County UPI certification fee?
faqs.a: It is $20.00 for each UPI certification, paid to Mercer County Tax Assessment rather than to the Recorder. Naming the parent parcel on a document carries no extra fee.

faqs.q: What is the base price of a Mercer County deed filing?
faqs.a: A deed starts at $71.25, which pays for four pages, four names and one parcel. Each added page runs $2.00, each added name or parcel $0.50, and the Statement of Value tacks on $2.00.

faqs.q: Can Mercer County recording fees go on a credit card?
faqs.a: No. The office takes cash or checks only. A check should show the account holder's current address and phone number.

faqs.q: Why is Hermitage transfer tax higher than the rest of Mercer County?
faqs.a: Hermitage and Sharon carry 2.5 percent local tax, while Farrell and Greenville charge 2 percent. Other places use the usual 1 percent local share on top of the 1 percent state tax.

faqs.q: When do new Mercer County property values take effect?
faqs.a: The reassessment was moved to the 2028 tax year. Owners will get a Final Value Mailer in 2027 explaining the new values and how to appeal.
